title: metadata-protocol: removing the second holder's .custom override of a shared name judges the pair row against a bare-name owner lookup, so it may depend on registration order (ADR-0150 D4)
body:
epic:#31527#1 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CYGYEUhpi29FpjLmxT

Part of #31527. Found as an unconfirmed side read by the contract review of PR #32507 (#31696 PR-3; review 6814434131, red-line read 6814441684, ruling 6814454746). It is outside that PR's diff.

**Suspected defect (read, not run).** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts:429` judges a pair-row removal (`<base>.custom`) against `packagedArtifactOwner`, a bare-name lookup. When two namespaces hold a name, for example a flow after #31696 lands, removing the second holder's `.custom` override may be judged against whichever holder registered first. It may then be refused, or the wrong holder's override removed. Under epic red line 2, it must be judged against the pair's own base.

**Premise re-check (run first).** With two packages A and B each holding flow `f` and each with a `.custom` override, register A first, then remove `?package=B.custom` for `f`. Expected: B's override removed, A's untouched. Run it in both registration orders. Zero difference between the orders means the premise is false; close the card.

**Fix direction if it reproduces.** Read the owner from the pair id's base (`isPairOf`) rather than from the bare name. Pin both registration orders.

Blocked-by: #31696
